newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice prices seen firm on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice prices seen firm on foreign demand.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are likely to rise next week on demand from exporters amid buoyant U.S. rice futures, dealers said on Thursday.

Prices of IRRI-6 variety firmed this week partly on demand from exporters and partly on rising U.S. rice futures, which have gone up on fears that adverse weather could cut the world rice crop, particularly in India, one exporter said.
He said Pakistan's domestic production was unlikely to be affected because sowing had been completed in April/May, with the harvest not due until September/October.
Basmati super export prices were rising slowly on expectations of higher demand from abroad, the exporter said.
An official of the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) said it had sold 2,500 tonnes of basmati Pak-7 rice at $441 per tonne FOB earlier this week.

He said the RECP had received four bids, the highest of which was $441 per tonne FOB, for the sale and export of 5,000 tonnes of basmati variety Pak-7 1996/97 (July-June) rice containing seven percent broken.
Other bidders had quoted $437, $437 and $436.75 per tonne FOB. An exporter said the RECP would probably reinvite bids for the remaining 2,500 tonnes of basmati later.
Pakistan exported 1.603 million tonnes of rice worth $431 million in the first 11 months of 1996/97 compared to 1.253 million worth $411 million in the same period a year ago.
In May, rice exports fell to 124,338 tonnes worth $37 million, compared to 185,349 tonnes worth $48 million in April and 119,565 tonnes worth $38 million in May 1996.
